answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post work or claim rewards. A verifier samples tasks and checks signed commitments; when linked identities submit the same fabricated result, a challenge can expose the duplicate and slash their stake. The jetty is the entry cost, the tide is repeated verification, and the bridge to influence is earned through useful work. A Sybil attacker must therefore buy and risk real capital for every identity, while honest agents can recover stake and build reputation.
